target.title: fix(commands): bound reset-hook transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBeforeResetTranscript` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` reads the previous session transcript with an unbounded `fs.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the reset-hook path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset-hook transcript reader is now routed through the existing streaming session transcript reader (`readSessionMessagesAsync`), which already caps reads and supports archive fallback. This avoids whole-file buffering while preserving previous-session messages for `before_reset` hooks.

`storePath` is forwarded into the reader scope and by both runtime callers:
- the normal `/new`/`/reset` command handlers in `commands-reset.ts`, and
- the missed-reset-hook fallback in `get-reply.ts`.

This keeps custom-store transcript resolution consistent across both entry points.

## User Impact

Reset hooks now receive previous session messages safely even for very large transcripts, without risking process OOM, and custom store paths continue to resolve correctly on both command and fallback paths.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests that mock `readSessionMessagesAsync` and verify the reader scope (`sessionId`, `sessionFile`, `sessionKey`, `storePath`, `agentId`) and the `allowResetArchiveFallback` option.
- Added focused coverage proving `storePath` is forwarded into the reader scope for custom-store sessions.
- Added fallback-caller coverage in `get-reply.reset-hooks-fallback.test.ts` proving `storePath` reaches `emitResetCommandHooks` when inline actions return early.
- Local focused runs pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts --run` (6/6 tests)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts --run` (12/12 tests)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.reset-hooks-fallback.test.ts --run` (3/3 tests)
- `oxlint` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the actual changed helper from source and exercises the real `emitResetCommandHooks` path with a patched global hook runner and an oversized transcript.

Script: `/tmp/proof-101479.mjs` (not committed).

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101479.mjs
=== Oversized transcript ===
Transcript file size: 16781943 bytes (cap is 16777216 bytes)
Hook fired: true
Hook event action: reset
Hook payload messages count: 3
First payload message role: user
Last payload message role: assistant
All messages preserved: true
```

The helper streams the transcript instead of buffering it whole, and the `before_reset` hook receives the full set of previous messages.

target.title: fix(config): cap legacy toolsBySender deprecation warning cache with shared dedupe helper
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded memory growth in legacy `toolsBySender` deprecation warning deduplication. The `warnedLegacyToolsBySenderKeys` Set accumulated every warned legacy sender key forever with no eviction, TTL, or size cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the unbounded `Set` with the existing `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })` helper from `src/infra/dedupe.ts`. The shared dedupe cache provides `check()` with touch-on-read, max-size pruning via `pruneMapToMaxSize`, and a TTL hook — no bespoke LRU stack needed.

## User Impact

No change for gateways handling fewer than 4096 distinct legacy `toolsBySender` keys. Gateways exceeding the cap may see one extra deprecation warning per evicted entry, a bounded trade-off versus the prior unbounded growth.

## Evidence

- `pnpm vitest run --project runtime-config src/config/group-policy.test.ts` — 21 passed
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/config/group-policy.ts src/config/group-policy.test.ts` — 0 warnings, 0 errors

### Live proof: 4096-entry dedupe cache with eviction and hot-key retention

```text
$ npx tsx live-proof.ts

=== Proof 1: Eviction of oldest entry past the 4096 cap ===

→ Fed 4096 distinct legacy keys through resolveToolsBySender.
→ Deprecation warnings emitted so far: 4096
→ After eviction, "legacy-key-1" re-warning: YES (as expected)

=== Proof 2: Hot-key retention (LRU touch-on-read) ===

→ Touched "hot-key" 42 times through resolveToolsBySender.
→ Warnings for "hot-key": 1 (expected: 1 — only first encounter).

=== Summary ===
4096-entry dedupe cache verified:
  1. Cache stays at 4096 entries maximum.
  2. Oldest untouched entries are evicted on overflow.
  3. Frequently re-warned entries survive via LRU touch-on-read.
```

target.title: fix(nextcloud-talk): strip internal tool-trace banners from outbound text
target.body:
Part of #90684

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Nextcloud Talk users receiving bot replies would see internal assistant tool-trace scaffolding lines (e.g. `⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed`) leaked into outbound messages. These banners are internal runtime diagnostics that should not reach end users.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Nextcloud Talk outbound adapter lacked a `sanitizeText` hook on `outbound.base`, so core `stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding` was the only sanitization layer — and it does not remove tool-trace failure banners. Adding `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` on the outbound `sanitizeText` hook matches the accepted sibling pattern already shipped for Slack, Signal, Matrix, Feishu, Mattermost, Telegram, Google Chat, QQBot, IRC, SMS, Discord, WhatsApp, and LINE. The hook is merged onto the resolved outbound adapter via `resolveChatChannelOutbound`.

## User Impact

Nextcloud Talk users no longer see internal tool-trace failure banners in bot replies. Normal assistant prose and markdown chunking behavior are preserved.

## Evidence

**Negative control — core strip keeps banner (pre-fix behavior):**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding } from "./src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text)));
console.log("Banner survives:", stripInternalRuntimeScaffolding(text).includes("⚠️"));'

Output: "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed"
Banner survives: true
```

**After fix — nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound.sanitizeText strips banner:**

```
$ node --import tsx -e '
import { nextcloudTalkPlugin } from "./extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/channel.js";
const text = "Done.\n⚠️ 🛠️ `search repos (agent)` failed";
const result = nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text, payload: { text } });
console.log("Output:", JSON.stringify(result));
console.log("Banner stripped:", !result?.includes("⚠️"));
const prose = "The pipeline has 3 open deals.";
const proseResult = nextcloudTalkPlugin.outbound?.sanitizeText?.({ text: prose, payload: { text: prose } });
console.log("Prose:", JSON.stringify(proseResult));
console.log("Prose unchanged:", proseResult === prose);'

Output: "Done."
Banner stripped: true
Prose: "The pipeline has 3 open deals."
Prose unchanged: true
```

**Focused test:**

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**Lint (changed files):**

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/channel.ts extensions/nextcloud-talk/src/outbound-tool-trace-sanitize.test.ts

(no findings)
```

Verified on branch `fix/nextcloud-talk-sanitize-outbound-90684` at `ccc41f12321`.

**What was not tested:** No live Nextcloud Talk round-trip — credentials were not available in this checkout. The bug is in the sanitization layer before network delivery, so the proof above covers the affected boundary without a live channel.

target.title: test(gateway): lock config mutation allowlist contract
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Gateway `config.patch` / `config.apply` mutations are guarded by an allowlist, but the contract was not locked in tests. A regression could silently widen or narrow which config paths agents may change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a focused contract test suite that exercises both the allowlist guard and the real `createGatewayTool().execute()` path for `config.patch` and `config.apply`, so future edits cannot drift without failing CI.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change for operators. Maintainers and contributors get a stable regression gate on gateway config mutation policy.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Gateway agent tool config mutations must reject protected paths and dangerous flags before RPC, and allow only allowlisted paths through `createGatewayTool` execution.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (Darwin), Node.js v22.22.0.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ gateway config mutation allowlist contract (12 tests)
 ✓ gateway tool config mutation execution path (4 tests)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  16 passed (16)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `createGatewayTool().execute()` with `config.patch` forwards allowlisted edits to RPC and rejects protected/dangerous paths before RPC; `config.apply` rejects protected wholesale replacements before RPC.
- **What was not tested:** Live gateway RPC against a running gateway instance; contract tests mock the RPC client and exercise the production guard + tool execution path.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/gateway-tool-allowlist.contract.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose`

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? No
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? No
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? No — tests only
- Highest-risk area: none (test-only PR)
- Mitigation: n/a

## AI-assisted disclosure

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor agent)
- [x] Human-run Real behavior proof from local setup

target.title: fix(commands): bound reset-hook transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBeforeResetTranscript` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` reads the previous session transcript with an unbounded `fs.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the reset-hook path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reset-hook transcript reader is now routed through the existing streaming session transcript reader (`readSessionMessagesAsync`), which already caps reads and supports archive fallback. This avoids whole-file buffering while preserving previous-session messages for `before_reset` hooks.

`storePath` is forwarded into the reader scope and by both runtime callers:
- the normal `/new`/`/reset` command handlers in `commands-reset.ts`, and
- the missed-reset-hook fallback in `get-reply.ts`.

This keeps custom-store transcript resolution consistent across both entry points.

## User Impact

Reset hooks now receive previous session messages safely even for very large transcripts, without risking process OOM, and custom store paths continue to resolve correctly on both command and fallback paths.

## Evidence

- Added regression tests that mock `readSessionMessagesAsync` and verify the reader scope (`sessionId`, `sessionFile`, `sessionKey`, `storePath`, `agentId`) and the `allowResetArchiveFallback` option.
- Added focused coverage proving `storePath` is forwarded into the reader scope for custom-store sessions.
- Added fallback-caller coverage in `get-reply.reset-hooks-fallback.test.ts` proving `storePath` reaches `emitResetCommandHooks` when inline actions return early.
- Local focused runs pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts --run` (6/6 tests)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts --run` (12/12 tests)
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply.reset-hooks-fallback.test.ts --run` (3/3 tests)
- `oxlint` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the actual changed helper from source and exercises the real `emitResetCommandHooks` path with a patched global hook runner and an oversized transcript.

Script: `/tmp/proof-101479.mjs` (not committed).

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101479.mjs
=== Oversized transcript ===
Transcript file size: 16781943 bytes (cap is 16777216 bytes)
Hook fired: true
Hook event action: reset
Hook payload messages count: 3
First payload message role: user
Last payload message role: assistant
All messages preserved: true
```

The helper streams the transcript instead of buffering it whole, and the `before_reset` hook receives the full set of previous messages.
